proven: Actual fb6 device build exit0/not timed out. Actual full-owned producer exit1/not timed out at full-application-package.py80: only four-byte thin64 magic was accepted. The failing executable path/magic was not included in that error.

Pinned checksum-matching Firebase input contains a static ar FMWK. Actual Xcode log14479–14515 removes static executable then injects a native MH_DYLIB stub and invokes lipo -create for exactly five framework destinations. This is not evidence that the final CI App contains ar executables.
Pinned Apple cctools lipo source builds FAT_MAGIC and writes its header even with one input for -create; only a different extract_family path has the single-input thin exception.

Production inventory/reader already distinguish FAT32/FAT64 and rigorously check each slice. Package preflight, the actual code transformer and full-S3 platform helper independently required thin64. Merely broadening or skipping the producer would leave actual production rejection.
diagnosis.inference: The recorded single-arm64 stub→lipo commands strongly explain a valid single-slice FAT32 wrapper rejected by the producer. Exact post-lipo CI binary bytes were not uploaded, so the actual offending file/header is not independently recovered.
diagnosis.notJustified: No evidence establishes a bad manual App embed configuration. Existing project has SPM framework linkage and only an explicit extension copy phase. Removing standard framework destinations, treating ar as executable Mach-O, skipping unknown components or stripping wrappers would obscure this failure and can lose resources/shape.

implementation: The existing Reader parses the complete original container. Only BE FAT32 with one little-endian64 arm64/subtype-low24zero slice terminating at the full file end is added. FAT64, multiple slices, swapped outer byte order, unknown/ar and unclassified trailing bytes still fail.

Complete supplied FAT32 bytes go through the existing content-hash/CMS verifier first. The same original thin transformer re-signs the sole validated slice with all original load-command, key/certificate, external slot, terminal signature and cancellation checks intact.

All pre-slice header/table/padding bytes are copied verbatim; only the fat_arch.size field is updated. CPU/subtype, sole architecture and offset are retained. The complete output including wrapper is bounded by the existing268MiB ceiling and independently re-read/hash/CMS-verified.

Result.originalSignatures/contentHashes/signatures use complete-file reader coordinates; signatureOffset is the output full-file signature.range.offset. The public async owner and thin transformation/crypto helper bytes are unchanged.

Package structural preflight admits only the existing verified single-arm64 thin/FAT32 structure. Before any scoped staged mutation, raw FAT32 must be BE. Existing child-first resource updates hash whole wrapped executable bytes; profile/lease/CAS/archive/final independent verification gates remain.

Full S3 platform checking uses the same structural reader to locate its unique slice, then retains the independent actual LC_BUILD_VERSION count/length/platforms==[IOS] check. No plist platform, deployment target, code bytes or permissions are patched.

testChanges.authoredPositive: Two existing genuinely CMS-signed thin fixtures, including large signature-tail shrinkage, wrapped in FAT32 with nonzero prefix padding; actual re-sign with changed CodeResources; full-file independent hash/CMS readback, retained prefix/offset/CPU and complete-file proof/signature coordinates.
testChanges.authoredNegative: Parsed FAT64, valid two-architecture container, parsed swapped FAT32, unclassified tail, real slice byte tamper and static ar all rejected; every prior malformed-layout/trust/encryption/cancellation vector retained.
testChanges.fullS3TestBody: byte exact; only existing platform helper changed

limits: These four Swift files are source-only candidates on Windows. The augmented cryptographic tests and same-job full iPhoneOS/JVM package test have not executed.
The actual fb6 failure and missing post-lipo bytes remain preserved. This does not turn the old run into signing success or prove these exact Swift APIs compile.

No new general fat/multiarchitecture signer, static archive parser, business owner, framework deletion or broad embed-policy change is introduced.
